text: The PII masking rule set is read as versioned reference data on the reference-data contract of rwb-case (the DP-07 default ruling) and applied inside rwb-debtsale as data; no masking pattern, default or predicate is written in code.
why: BR-S6-003 forbids a value a business person may change from being written in code, and no source gives the content of the rule set, so it can only be read with its version and recorded with the outcome.
read: The rule set is read at its version in step 3 of section 4, its version is written into the decision record (BR9), an unversioned rule set holds the step (X6), and DP-07 is recorded as an absent pattern row of the key rather than added to the metadata.
confirm: Solution architect and the owner of the reference data of rwb-case
impact: The tape step can start on Day 1 against a versioned rule set and its fake; the rule set's content stays open and no masking behaviour is fixed until the owner publishes it

text: The account and borrower facts the tape carries are read at build time on the rwb-source-data data product with its as-of date, masked inside the activity and never written to rwb_debtsale; this service holds no v_ace_* grant and no ACE table grant.
why: The legacy feature read the ACE database in-process, only rwb-source-data holds the 30 v_ace_* views in the target, and the plan's pattern set carries no DP-05 row although the step needs the fact.
read: Step 4 of section 4 reads the fact on the owner's contract with a 2 s budget and a breaker, BR3 states the prohibition, the stale path is X4 with MSG-P1-001, the Data section marks the ACE rows as not read, and the boundary test of section 13 fails any statement that reaches an ACE table or a v_ace_* view.
confirm: Owner of rwb-source-data and the solution architect
impact: No personal fact is persisted in rwb_debtsale and the tape can be built as soon as the data product and its fake are published

text: The masked tape is stored once as a claim-check file through the rwb-document contract on Blob with WORM, and its document reference, size, checksum and masking-check result are held in the local decision record and on the document metadata, because no table or column of rwb_debtsale carries a tape reference.
why: R-DS-10 names the Document Hub and the FSD names the file per lot, the Ownership Map gives S6 two business tables and neither has a document, tape or tape-status column, and the plan declares no DB story of this key.
read: Step 9 of section 4 writes the file in the same transaction as the record, BR1 forbids a second copy, section 11 places the reference and checksum in the decision record, section 12.7 lists decision_record as the holder, and the data room of RWB-S6-E5026-APP reads the same document on the owner's contract.
confirm: Owner of rwb-document and the solution architect
impact: The tape has one home and one reference; a later DB or API change that adds a tape column would move the reference and must keep the decision record as the audit trail

text: The 'PII service' of the FSD has no row among the 19 services; its two duties, the masking rules and the masking check, are the versioned reference-data read and a check executed inside rwb-debtsale, so no separate masking service is called and none is invented.
why: The FSD names the PII service as an integration point and in the Systems column of R-DS-10 and R-DS-11, the S6 context pack owns no such row and the Architecture v5 service list contains none.
read: The rule set of ASM-B2-S6-015-1 and the check of R-DS-11 both sit in this service's step, section 2 records the absent mapping, section 8 reads the Systems column as the rule set and the check, and section 19 puts the mapping out of scope with this citation.
confirm: Solution architect and the platform owner
impact: No cross-service call is added for masking; if the platform later provides a PII service, the check is replaced by a C row and the story keeps its behaviour

text: The tape column list, its file format and its tape spec version are fixed by no source; the build follows a versioned tape spec derived from the lot and account fields DF-SAL-020 to DF-SAL-037 plus the masked personal set, and every column is read from the spec at its version rather than coded.
why: The FSD defines the feature as 'builds the data tape' without a layout, the TSD defines no tape object, the S6 context pack gives the service two business tables (neither a tape) and the legacy endpoints row says the work runs inside the module with no interface.
read: Step 5 of section 4 lays the tape out under the spec version, the Data section marks the masked field set and the column list as not specified, BR5 and BR9 make the spec version a versioned input recorded with the outcome, and X6 holds the step when no version is in force.
confirm: Business owner of debt sale and the solution architect
impact: The story builds a versioned tape spec and can be demonstrated on a synthetic fixture; the real buyer-facing layout waits for the owner's sign-off

text: The operation names of the rwb-source-data facts read, the rwb-document file write, the rwb-case case-move answer, the rwb-case reference-data read and the rwb-decision package read are not published in the sources; they are consumed as class C rows with placeholders and stubbed fakes and are not added to the plan's empty C row.
why: The plan fixes the H, C, I and X rows of every slice and a worker may not rewrite them, yet the step cannot run without those five rows and no source publishes their operation names.
read: The five rows sit in 12.2 with the placeholder, their fakes sit in 12.8, section 13 states that they are class C rows the plan does not hold, and every placeholder pairs this combined gap row with this assumption.
confirm: Owners of rwb-source-data, rwb-document, rwb-case and rwb-decision
impact: The story starts on Day 1 against documents and fakes; the dependency map under-reports five rows until the owners confirm their operation names
